answers.how: Replace the proof's `mem.is_symlink() and mem.resolve() == clone` with a check that accepts a symlink or (os.name == 'nt') a reparse point whose resolve() equals the clone; it must still red when the dir is a plain directory or a link to somewhere else. The proof's red-first teeth plant a plain dir and a link elsewhere.
answers.title: the memory-link proof asks whether the memory dir is a link the way memory_link does, so a Windows junction counts
answers.traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof red on one OS for a platform reason, not a behaviour reason, is not measuring the component; Law 9: the red is a distance from the spec and this one is the proof's own; CP4.
answers.what: The proof's link check accepts what memory_link.py makes on each OS: a symlink, or on nt a junction, that resolves to the clone.
